details: Recent softer-than-expected US inflation data, specifically the August Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, has significantly reduced market expectations for a Federal Reserve interest rate hike in October 2026. The annual PCE index rose by 3.4%, below the anticipated 3.7%, with core inflation at 3.0% against a forecast of 3.3%. Federal Reserve Vice Chair Philip Jefferson and New York Fed President John Williams have indicated that policymakers may need more time to assess incoming data before making further rate adjustments. This shift has led to a decrease in the probability of an October rate hike, currently estimated to be below 40-50% by prediction markets, down from approximately 70% previously. This development is generally viewed as favorable for risk assets, including cryptocurrencies.
title: Federal Reserve Signals Potential Pause in October Rate Hikes

details: Isabel Schnabel, a member of the European Central Bank (ECB) board, has stated the necessity for central bank money to transition "onchain." This move aims to prevent tokenized markets from exclusively settling in private or foreign-currency assets, thereby maintaining central bank influence and stability within the evolving digital financial landscape. The ECB has further detailed three potential models for integrating central bank money into blockchain-based systems.
title: ECB Advocates for Onchain Central Bank Money Amid Tokenized Market Growth

details: Regulatory clarity and integration efforts for cryptocurrencies are progressing across various jurisdictions. The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has proposed dedicated custody standards for registered investment advisers and regulated funds holding crypto assets. Concurrently, the U.S. Congress is considering expanding crypto rules for banks, credit unions, and stablecoins, with the Congressional Research Service providing context on Bitcoin policies for banks. In the UK, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) has begun permitting applications for authorization from crypto firms, bringing them under clearer regulatory standards. Additionally, South African bank Absa Group has launched digital-asset custody services on the XRP Ledger. These moves signal a continued trend toward institutional involvement and a more regulated crypto environment.
title: Global Regulatory Bodies Advance Crypto Oversight and Integration

details: Following the release of the lower-than-expected US inflation data on September 30, Bitcoin experienced a brief surge, pushing its price above $85,000. This positive reaction was consistent with market expectations that easing inflationary pressures could lead to a less aggressive stance from the Federal Reserve regarding interest rates. However, Bitcoin subsequently retraced some of these gains, with prices on October 2nd showing Bitcoin at approximately $85,956 and Ethereum at $2,717, amid ongoing pressures from factors like rising Treasury yields and oil prices.
title: Bitcoin Briefly Surges Past $85,000 on Inflation Data, Then Retraces
